query: For bulk HfNbTaTiZr, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified predictive approach make to overcome the limited accuracy of available analytical predictions and their usual restriction to perfect, defect-free crystals? Address the nearly 0–200 K regime and the 300–1200 K regime, for which measurements also exist on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen; explain why the approach should improve accuracy, predict its advantage over existing analytical approaches, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a held-out conductivity benchmark and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: An integrated predictive approach that combines ab initio techniques, active-learning based moment-tensor potentials, and Bayesian correction for defect effects (e.g., oxygen-induced lattice perturbations) can yield thermal/electrical conductivity predictions for bulk HfNbTaTiZr with 1 wt.% oxygen that more accurately match experimental measurements in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes compared to conventional analytical models which assume perfect crystals.
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy synthesized via powder metallurgy routes with a measured oxygen impurity level of approximately 1 wt.%.
generation.intervention: Implement a predictive framework that assimilates ab initio data with machine-learning corrections to account for oxygen-related defects, integrating moment-tensor potentials within a Bayesian optimization workflow; then use this model to predict the material's conductivity across the specified temperature regimes.
generation.conditions: Temperature regimes from 0–200 K (cryogenic behavior) and 300–1200 K (elevated temperature behavior) under ambient pressure conditions, using specimens with approximately 1 wt.% oxygen impurity.
generation.structural_mediator: The presence of oxygen at defect sites and any resultant local lattice distortions (e.g., grain boundary modifications, local bonding variations) which alter phonon and electron scattering pathways.
generation.mechanism: Oxygen impurities introduce localized disruptions and defect states that modify lattice vibrations and electronic scattering events; by incorporating these effects through Bayesian-calibrated, active-learned potentials, the new approach adjusts for deviations from perfect-crystal behavior, thereby improving conductivity predictions.
generation.predicted_outcome: The new predictive model will reduce the prediction error of conductivity values to below ~10% discrepancy compared to experimental measurements in both the low (0–200 K) and high temperature (300–1200 K) regimes, outperforming conventional analytical approaches that may deviate by over 20% when neglecting defect effects.
generation.baseline: Existing analytical models assuming perfect, defect-free crystals which show significant prediction errors (potentially >20%) in conductivity measurements when applied to samples with 1 wt.% oxygen.
generation.boundary: The model is specifically applicable to HfNbTaTiZr alloys with low-level oxygen contamination (~1 wt.%) and within the temperature ranges of 0–200 K and 300–1200 K; applicability outside these oxygen levels or temperature ranges is presently unvalidated.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative improvement in predictive accuracy is uncertain and may depend on the precise manner in which oxygen defects affect scattering mechanisms; uncertainties also remain regarding the sensitivity of the employed machine-learning corrections to varying defect distributions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare bulk HfNbTaTiZr samples with verified 1 wt.% oxygen content and measure their electrical/thermal conductivity across the temperature ranges 0–200 K and 300–1200 K using standard methods (e.g., four-probe electrical measurements and laser flash analysis for thermal conductivity). Compare these experimental values against the predictions generated by (a) the conventional analytical model (assuming defect-free crystals) and (b) the new integrated predictive model.
measurements: Conductivity vs. temperature data across 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Error analysis between model predictions and experimental measurements.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the integrated predictive approach does not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in prediction error (e.g., achieving less than ~10% discrepancy compared to the >20% discrepancy of conventional approaches) in either the low or high temperature regime, then the hypothesis is falsified.

## Abstract
While first-principles methods have been successfully applied to characterize individual properties of multi-principal element alloys (MPEA), their use in searching for optimal trade-offs between competing properties is hampered by high computational demands. In this work, we present a framework to explore Pareto-optimal compositions by integrating advanced ab initio-based techniques into a Bayesian multi-objective optimization workflow, complemented by a simple analytical model providing straightforward analysis of trends. We benchmark the framework by applying it to solid solution strengthening and ductility of refractory MPEAs, with the parameters of the strengthening and ductility models being efficiently computed using a combination of the coherent-potential approximation method, accounting for finite-temperature effects, and actively-learned moment-tensor potentials parameterized with ab initio data. ## Abstract
AbstractHigh entropy alloys (HEA) have been one of the most attractive groups of materials for researchers in the last several years. Since HEAs are potential candidates for many (e.g., refractory, cryogenic, medical) applications, their properties are studied intensively. The most frequent method of HEA synthesis is arc or induction melting. Powder metallurgy is a perspective technique of alloy synthesis and therefore in this work the possibilities of synthesis of HfNbTaTiZr HEA from powders were studied. Blended elemental powders were sintered, hot isostatically pressed, and subsequently swaged using a special technique of swaging where the sample is enveloped by a titanium alloy. This method does not result in a full density alloy due to cracking during swaging. Spark plasma sintering (SPS) of mechanically alloyed powders resulted in a fully dense but brittle specimen. The most promising result was obtained by SPS treatment of gas atomized powder with low oxygen content.
